1.title: Risk Management Concepts
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Risk Management Concepts. It covers the exam area one. Security Principles. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. one point two Understand risk management concepts: Risk management lifecycle. Risk management processes. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Security Principles (twenty-four percent). Exam format: an adaptive exam of one hundred to one hundred twenty-five questions in two hours; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official I S C two C C exam outline.

1.title: Risk vocabulary
1.text: Risk vocabulary. The figure shows this: Risk is the chance that a threat uses a vulnerability to harm an asset.

1.title: Risk vocabulary, continued
1.text: Risk vocabulary. Asset. Anything of value to the organization: data, systems, people, reputation. Threat. A possible cause of harm: an attacker, malware, a flood. Vulnerability. A weakness that a threat can use: unpatched software, weak password. Likelihood. How probable it is that the threat uses the weakness. Impact. The harm if it happens: money, downtime, law, trust. Risk. The chance of loss: likelihood combined with impact. Exposure. Being open to a threat through a vulnerability. You cannot remove all risk. The goal is to bring risk within what the organization accepts. Exam tip: A threat needs a vulnerability to cause risk. A vulnerability with no threat, or a threat with no vulnerability, gives little risk.

1.title: The risk management lifecycle
1.text: The risk management lifecycle. Risk management is a repeating cycle, not a one-time project. one Identify. Find the assets, threats and vulnerabilities. two Assess. Estimate likelihood and impact and rank the risks. three Treat. Choose a response for each risk (section four). four Monitor and review. Track the risk, test the controls, repeat as things change. Results go into a risk register: a list of risks with an owner, a rating, the treatment and the status. Key risk indicators (K R Is) are measures that warn that risk is rising (Module six).

1.title: Assessing risk
1.text: Assessing risk. Qualitative. How: Rate by judgment: low, medium, high; a risk matrix. Result: Fast, subjective. Quantitative. How: Use money and numbers. Result: Precise, needs data. Asset value (A V). What the asset is worth. Exposure factor (E F). The percent of the asset lost in one event. Single loss expectancy (S L E). A V times E F: the loss from one event. Annualized rate of occurrence (A R O). How many times a year the event is expected. Annualized loss expectancy (A L E). S L E times A R O: the expected loss per year.

1.title: Assessing risk, continued
1.text: Assessing risk. Example: A V of one hundred thousand dollars and E F of fifty percent give an S L E of fifty thousand; with an A R O of zero point two (once in five years) the A L E is ten thousand dollars per year. A safeguard is worth buying when it costs less than the A L E it removes. Exam tip: S L E equals A V times E F. A L E equals S L E times A R O. Do qualitative first when numbers are missing.

1.title: Risk treatment
1.text: Risk treatment. Avoid. Meaning: Stop the activity that creates the risk. Example: Do not store card numbers at all. Mitigate (reduce). Meaning: Add controls to lower likelihood or impact. Example: Patch, encrypt, train staff. Transfer (share). Meaning: Move the financial impact to someone else. Example: Insurance, a contract with a provider. Accept. Meaning: Live with the risk knowingly. Example: Low risk, or the control costs more than the loss. Two key limits: risk appetite is how much risk the organization is willing to take to reach its goals; risk tolerance is the acceptable variation around it.

1.title: Risk treatment, continued
1.text: Risk treatment. Inherent risk. The risk before controls. Residual risk. The risk that remains after controls; it must be accepted by management. Exam tip: Insurance transfers the cost, not the responsibility. Residual risk is accepted by management, not by the security team alone.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A server runs unpatched software that a known worm can use. In risk terms, what is the unpatched software? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A vulnerability that a threat can use. A weakness that a threat can use is a vulnerability; the worm is the threat.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A company buys cyber insurance to cover the cost of a breach. Which risk treatment is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Transfer of the financial impact. Insurance moves the financial impact to another party, which is risk transfer.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A project would store card numbers that the business does not really need. The team decides not to store them. Which treatment is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Avoidance, because the activity is stopped. Stopping the activity that creates the risk is avoidance.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An asset is worth two hundred thousand dollars and a flood would destroy twenty-five percent of it. What is the single loss expectancy? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: fifty thousand dollars, from asset value times exposure factor. S L E equals asset value times exposure factor, two hundred thousand times zero point two five.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. After controls are applied, some risk remains. Who should formally accept this residual risk? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Management, who owns the business risk. Residual risk is accepted by management, which owns the business risk.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A team rates each risk as low, medium or high on a matrix, without money values. Which assessment method is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Qualitative analysis using judgment and ratings. Ratings and a risk matrix are qualitative assessment.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What are the four risk treatment options? Answer: Avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept. Question two. What is the formula for annualized loss expectancy? Answer: S L E times A R O. Question three. What is residual risk? Answer: The risk that remains after controls.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is a risk register? Answer: A list of risks with owners, ratings, treatments and status. Question five. What is risk appetite? Answer: How much risk the organization is willing to take. Question six. Does the risk cycle end? Answer: No, it repeats: identify, assess, treat, monitor.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Risk: threat uses a vulnerability to harm an asset; likelihood and impact. Lifecycle: identify, assess, treat, monitor and review; repeat. Qualitative or quantitative: ratings and matrix or money values. Formulas: S L E equals A V times E F; A L E equals S L E times A R O. Treatments: avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept.
